**Company Description**
By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.
  
  
**Why join Harvard Medical School?**
Harvard Medical School's mission is to nurture a diverse, inclusive community dedicated to alleviating suffering and improving health and well-being for all through excellence in teaching and learning, discovery and scholarship, and service and leadership.
  
  
You’ll be at the heart of biomedical discovery, education, and innovation, working alongside world-renowned faculty and a community dedicated to improving human health. This is more than a job - it’s an opportunity to shape the future of medicine.
  
  
**About the Department of Immunology:**
Position open for a Scientific AI Engineer, to work in the context of the ImmGen consortium at Harvard Medical School. ImmGen is an NIH-funded consortium of Immunology and Computational biology labs who pool expertise to decipher gene expression and it regulation in the immune system, whose data have become a valuable resource for the Immunology research community worldwide. The group wishes to develop a data analysis AI agent that will harness ImmGen data together with external databases to answer user questions formulated by scientists in natural language and return data-grounded visualizations and contextualization.
  
  
**Job Description**
We are seeking an autonomous Scientific AI Engineer who will work closely with the existing ImmGen computational team and immunologists to design and implement this agent. They will integrate ImmGen’s existing data resources and analytical capabilities with the AI-powered interface. They will not be expected to acquire or manage ImmGen data, nor rebuild analytical tools. Instead, they will determine how to expose, adapt, orchestrate, and extend those tools so they can be reliably accessed through natural-language interaction, using MCP strategies that can be exploited by AI agents.
  
  
**The position will:**

* Work closely with ImmGen scientists and data analysts to understand existing datasets, metadata, documentation, tools, APIs, and access mechanisms, adapt and wrap existing ImmGen data so they can be invoked reliably by LLM-based agent that calls on public analytical and visualization tools.
* Collaborate with ImmGen scientists to define supported use cases, desired answer formats, and appropriate scientific language and graphics.
* Map existing and potential researcher questions to the appropriate existing ImmGen resources and analytical workflows.
* Develop the software interfaces, APIs, schemas, computational guardrails and orchestration logic required to connect the agent to ImmGen’s existing infrastructure.
* Implement safeguards against hallucinated results, invalid comparisons, inappropriate statistical interpretations, and unsupported biological claims.
* Ensure that the agent does not automatically initiate unduly expensive computes.
* We are looking for a team player eager to participate in the exciting re-writing of scientific data propagation.

**Qualifications**
**Basic Qualifications:**

* Minimum of five years’ post-secondary education or relevant work experience.

**Additional Qualifications and Skills:**

* Advanced degree or equivalent professional experience in computational biology, bioinformatics, genomics, or a related field.
* Strong Python programming skills and experience with scientific computing libraries such as pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, Scanpy, Bioconductor, or equivalent tools.
* Strong software-engineering skills, including experience with APIs, data schemas, testing, version control, logging, documentation, and reproducible workflows.
* Experience integrating software with existing scientific data platforms, analytical pipelines, web services, or computational tools.
* Hands-on experience with LLM applications, including tool/function calling, retrieval-augmented generation, structured outputs, agent orchestration, or natural-language-to-SQL/code systems.

About Vercel:
  
  
Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.
  
  
Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide.
  
  
About the role:
  
  
Agents are becoming first-class users of the internet. They sign in, call APIs, deploy code, and act on behalf of people and teams. That raises questions the web was never designed to answer: Who is this agent? Who does it work for? What is it allowed to do, for how long, and how do we know?
  
  
As an engineer on the Agent Auth and Identity team, you'll help answer those questions. You'll build the systems that let agents and people authenticate, delegate access, and act safely across Vercel and the services our customers connect to. This is foundational work: identity and authorization sit underneath everything we ship, and getting them right for agents will shape how modern software gets built.
  
  
The scope is intentionally broad. You might spend one quarter designing how credentials are issued and scoped for autonomous agents, and the next building the developer-facing APIs and SDKs that make secure auth feel effortless. You'll own systems end-to-end, from design through long-term operation in production.
  
  
We're looking for engineers who care deeply about security and developer experience in equal measure, enjoy working on problems without established playbooks, and want to define how trust works in an agentic world. This is a hybrid role based in San Francisco, in the office on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday.
  
  
What you'll do:
  
  

* Design, build, and operate the identity, authentication, and authorization systems that power Vercel and our Customers for both people and agents.
* Shape how agents prove who they are, act on behalf of users and teams, and receive scoped, time-bound, auditable access.
* Build secure, scalable APIs, services, and SDKs that make auth simple for developers and their agents to adopt.
* Work with modern and emerging standards (such as OAuth 2.x, OIDC, and agent-focused protocols) and help influence where they go next.
* Lead projects end-to-end: identify opportunities, set technical direction, and deliver improvements in security, reliability, and developer experience.
* Participate in the on-call rotation, taking responsibility for the reliability of critical systems.

What you need:
  
  

* 3+ years of experience designing, building, and operating backend systems in production at scale.
* Strong proficiency in JavaScript/TypeScript, or a comparable backend language and the willingness to work primarily in TypeScript.
* Solid understanding of authentication and authorization concepts, such as sessions, tokens, OAuth/OIDC flows, permission models, and secrets management.
* A security-minded approach to engineering: you think about threat models, least privilege, and failure modes as part of design, not as an afterthought.

Benefits & Compensation:
  
  

* Competitive compensation package, including equity.
* Inclusive Healthcare Package.
* Learn and Grow: we provide mentorship and send you to events that help you build your network and skills.
* Flexible Time Off.
* We will provide you the gear you need to do your role, and a WFH budget for you to outfit your space as needed.

Context Labs is seeking an early-career Data Scientist to support the deployment of Context Labs’ Decarbonization as a Service™ platform, built on our Immutably™ Data Fabric technology.

This role sits at the intersection of data science, engineering, and scientific computing. You will work with complex, real-world energy and emissions data and collaborate with application engineers, data engineers, and product teams to translate engineering methodologies and research ideas into robust, scalable analytical capabilities.

We do not expect you to arrive knowing every technology, emissions methodology, or aspect of the energy industry. We do expect strong quantitative reasoning, Python and SQL skills, and the curiosity and initiative to learn unfamiliar technical subjects and take ownership of challenging problems. This position reports to the Data Science Architect.

:**

* Work with domain experts to understand engineering and emissions methodologies, assumptions, and requirements and translate them into computational solutions.
* Develop, implement, validate, and document robust and reproducible emissions calculations and analytical methodologies.
* Explore complex customer datasets, understand their structure and meaning, identify data-quality issues, and investigate discrepancies.
* Implement scalable analytical workflows using Python, SQL, and PySpark, working with data engineers to move solutions into repeatable production workflows
* Help generalize customer-specific calculations, research ideas, and analytical prototypes into reusable software and product capabilities.
* Apply statistical methods to validate results, quantify uncertainty, and understand the limitations of available data and methodologies.
* Work within an ontology- and knowledge-graph-based framework to connect data to the entities, relationships, and concepts they represent.
* Write maintainable, modular Python code and contribute through Git, code review, testing, and documentation.
* Apply machine learning methods, including regression, classification, time-series analysis, and anomaly detection, when appropriate to the problem.
* Collaborate across Data Science, Data Engineering, Application Engineering, Product, R&D, and Customer Experience teams.
* Anything else as may reasonably be required by the company.

**What we’re looking for
:**

* Relevant professional experience in data science, scientific computing, engineering analytics, or related quantitative work. Candidates with an advanced degree and substantial applied research or project experience will also be considered.
* Strong Python and SQL skills, including experience developing maintainable, modular code beyond exploratory notebooks and working with complex, real-world datasets.
* Strong quantitative and analytical problem-solving skills, including comfort reasoning about equations, assumptions, data relationships, and statistical results.
* Working knowledge of statistics, including distributions, descriptive statistics, regression, and statistical validation.
* Experience investigating messy or heterogeneous datasets, identifying data-quality issues, and developing defensible analytical approaches.
* Familiarity with collaborative software-development practices such as Git, code review, testing, and documentation.
* Strong initiative and demonstrated ability to learn unfamiliar technical subjects, ask effective questions, seek out relevant expertise, and progressively take ownership of new problems.
* Ability to communicate analytical approaches, assumptions, and results clearly to technical and non-technical colleagues.
* BS or MS degree in Engineering, Physics, Applied Mathematics, Data Science, or another related quantitative scientific or technical discipline

**Bonus if you have
:**

* Experience working with energy, utilities, industrial, environmental, or emissions-related data, including greenhouse-gas or methane analytics.
* Familiarity with engineering or physical-system concepts such as mass and energy balances, thermodynamics, or process modeling.
* Experience with PySpark, Spark, Delta Lake, or other distributed data-processing technologies.
* Experience with uncertainty quantification, Monte Carlo methods or implementing scientific, engineering, or regulatory calculation methodologies in software.
* Knowledge of ontologies, knowledge graphs, or semantic modeling.

**Why you’ll like it here:**

* Context Labs is collaborative at its core. You’ll work within your team and across the organization allowing for continuous learning and discovery.
* We set goals that matter and provide value in all that we do, from building meaningful products to positively impacting carbon reduction and climate change.

**Who we are:**

Context Labs builds industrial AI data infrastructure for global markets, giving energy and industrial companies trusted data and AI outputs they can defend. Its platform turns fragmented operational and emissions data into continuously proven information, while sensitive data stays within each company’s own environment. Because the data is verified and the workflows validated, one platform can support any output, from carbon management and compliance to commercial use. The company grew out of research at MIT and is led by a team that helped build the internet at scale through earlier companies. Context Labs has offices in Amsterdam, Cambridge, Mass., and Houston, TX. Learn more at www.contextlabs.com.
